ecommerce.desc: If you sell on Amazon, Shopify, or Etsy, you're writing the same categories of copy over and over: listing titles, bullet points, A+ Content, ad copy, review responses. This pack gives you 10 tested prompt templates that turn a blank page into a first draft in under 2 minutes, no prompt engineering experience required.
includes: Product listing title + bullet point generator
A+ Content / Enhanced Brand Content module copy
Customer service email templates (refunds, delays, damage)
ecommerce.who: Amazon, Shopify and Etsy sellers, e-commerce VAs and brand managers.
faq: Will this work for my product category?
Yes. Every prompt has fill-in-the-blank fields, so it adapts to any product.

real-estate.desc: Between listing copy, buyer follow-ups, market updates, and objection handling, real estate agents write constantly, and most of it follows a pattern. This pack turns that pattern into 10 reusable prompts so you spend less time drafting and more time in front of clients.
includes: Just listed / just sold social post generator
Seller listing presentation talking points (CMA narrative)
real-estate.who: Listing agents, buyer's agents and small teams.
faq: Prompts are built with Fair Housing language guidelines in mind, but always review output before publishing.
Can I use this for luxury or commercial?
Yes. Adjust the tone field in each prompt.

insurance.desc: Independent agents and brokers lose hours to client emails that all follow the same shape: renewal reminders, policy explainers, life-event outreach. This pack gives you 10 prompts built with compliance guardrails in mind (no guaranteed-outcome language), so drafts are closer to send-ready from the start.
insurance.who: Life, health, auto and P&C agents and brokers.
faq: No. Every template is a drafting starting point; your agency's compliance process still applies before anything goes to a client.

legal.desc: Built for paralegals and case managers, not for legal strategy. This pack focuses on the high-volume communication work: turning messy intake notes into clean summaries, writing status updates that reduce anxious phone calls, and requesting missing documents clearly the first time.
legal.who: Paralegals, case managers and legal assistants at personal injury and immigration firms.
faq: No. These are communication templates; all output requires attorney review before reaching a client.
Is it safe to use with client information?
Use placeholders, not real client names or case numbers, in the AI tool itself. Fill in specifics afterward in your secure system.

events.desc: Solo planners and small studios juggle vendor coordination and client hand-holding at the same time. This pack covers both sides: the operational emails (vendor inquiries, timelines, confirmations) and the relationship-building ones (proposals, check-ins, difficult conversations).
events.who: Wedding planners, event planners and small planning studios.

fitness.desc: Coaching businesses are capped by how much time you spend writing instead of coaching. This pack covers the full client lifecycle, from onboarding through weekly check-ins to renewal, so every client feels personally attended to, even when you're using a template as the starting point.
fitness.who: Online and in-person fitness and nutrition coaches.
faq: Is the nutrition content medical advice?
No. General wellness guidance only, not for clients with diagnosed medical conditions.

recruiting.desc: Agency recruiters and in-house HR teams write constantly under time pressure: job descriptions, sourcing outreach, rejections, offer communications. This pack gives you send-ready drafts across the full hiring funnel, from first outreach to post-placement check-in.
recruiting.who: Agency recruiters, in-house recruiters and HR generalists.

finance.desc: Advisors write recurring client communications that carry real compliance weight: market updates, portfolio review talking points, social content. This pack is structured to avoid performance predictions and guaranteed-outcome language by default, so drafts start closer to compliant, though your firm's review process still applies.
finance.who: RIAs, independent advisors and wealth management associates.
faq: Is this compliant out of the box?
Every template avoids predictions and guarantees by design, but final compliance review by your firm is still required before anything reaches a client.

property.desc: Property managers handle the same categories of tenant communication across every unit: welcome emails, maintenance acknowledgments, rent notices, move-out instructions. This pack standardizes the tone across all of it: professional and clear, whether the news is good or not.
property.who: Residential property managers and landlords managing multiple units.

medical.desc: Practice admins handle patient communication constantly, and every message carries HIPAA weight. This pack is built around placeholder-based prompts (you never paste real patient information into the AI tool itself), covering everything from appointment reminders to insurance appeal letter drafts.
medical.who: Practice managers, front office staff and billing coordinators.
faq: The templates use placeholders instead of real patient data by design; you fill in specifics only inside your secure practice management system, never in the AI chat.
